Help-center excerpts:

[fee-refunds] Asking for a fee refund (effective 2025-01-01)
Support can refund some fees. There are two kinds of refund.

## Fees charged in error

If we charged a fee your plan doesn't have, or charged the same fee twice, we refund it. There's no limit on these refunds and they don't count toward anything else.

## Goodwill refunds

Once in any rolling 12-month period, support can refund one fee of up to $25.00 as a courtesy, even if it was charged correctly. That covers ATM fees, foreign transaction fees, card replacement and expedited shipping fees, wire fees and cash deposit fees.

Plan

[plan-fee-refunds] Refunds of plan fees (effective 2025-01-01)
minutes.

## What isn't refunded

Outside the cooling-off period, plan fees aren't refunded or prorated. That includes the month in which you downgrade and the month in which you close your account.

## How to ask

Message support in the app and say you'd like to cancel your paid plan under the cooling-off period. Support can process it for you straight away.

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any hour.

[plan-change] Changing your plan (effective 2025-01-01)
plan gets you a full refund of that charge. See "Refunds of plan fees".

There's no limit on how often you can change plans.

Need more help? Message us in the app any time, day or night.

[support-what-we-can-do] What our support team can help with (effective 2025-01-01)
Our support team can sort out most things during your chat. Some requests go to a specialist team, and a few things we can't do at all.

## Support can

- Freeze or unfreeze your card
- Report a card lost or stolen and order a replacement
- Open a dispute that's inside its window, has posted, and totals up to $5,000
- Refund a fee under our refund policy
- Change your plan
- Close your account if the balance is zero and nothing is pending or disputed
- Explain fees, limits and policies

##

[fee-refunds] Asking for a fee refund (effective 2025-01-01)
card replacement and expedited shipping fees, wire fees and cash deposit fees.

Plan fees aren't eligible for goodwill refunds. They have their own cooling-off rule instead.

## What support can't do

Support can't refund a second fee as goodwill within 12 months, can't refund a single fee above $25.00 as goodwill, and can't make exceptions to these rules. If you think a fee was charged in error, tell us why and we'll check.

## How to ask

Open the fee in your activity feed, tap Get help, and choose Question about a fee.

[fee-refunds] Asking for a fee refund (effective 2025-01-01)
in your activity feed, tap Get help, and choose Question about a fee. Refunds show up in your balance right away.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.

[support-what-we-can-do] What our support team can help with (effective 2025-01-01)
teams reply within 2 business days.

## Support can't

- Act for, or share details with, anyone other than the account holder
- Give investment, tax or legal advice
- Raise limits
- Refund fees outside the refund policy, or open disputes after their window

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any hour.

[disputes-subscriptions] Subscriptions that keep charging (effective 2026-01-15)
refund you, dispute each charge made after you cancelled. Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Cancelled but still charged. You have 120 days from each transaction date.

## Stopping future charges

If a merchant keeps charging after you cancel, you can report the card lost and get a new number. Recurring payments to the old number will then fail. There may be a replacement fee depending on your plan.

## Free trials

Charges after a free trial ended aren't unauthorized if you gave your card when signing up. Cancel with the merchant and ask for a refund.

Customer question:
Can support refund my monthly Plus fee as a one time courtesy thing?

You are the help-center assistant for Tallowbrook, a US neobank. Answer the customer's question using only the help-center excerpts you are given.

Rules:
- Use only facts stated in the excerpts. Do not add fees, limits, dates, steps or products they do not mention.
- Some excerpts are older versions of a policy. When two excerpts disagree, follow the one with the later effective date.
- If the question depends on the customer's plan (Basic, Plus or Premium), use that plan's numbers.
- If the question rests on something false (for example a fee that does not exist), say so and give the correct facts. That is an answer, not an abstention.
- Abstain when the excerpts do not contain the answer, when the question is not about Tallowbrook, or when it asks for investment, tax or legal advice. Set "abstain" to true and say briefly that the help center does not cover it.
- Cite the article IDs (the text in square brackets) of every excerpt you used. Cite nothing when you abstain.
- Keep the answer short: two to four sentences, plain language.

response.text: {"answer":"No. Monthly plan fees aren’t eligible for goodwill refunds; they have a separate cooling-off rule. Outside that period, plan fees aren’t refunded or prorated.","citations":["fee-refunds","plan-fee-refunds"],"abstain":false}
